cases.purpose: Exercise target-path observations across same-directory replacement publication.
cases.distinct_invariant: A coordinated concurrent observer sees the complete original and then the complete validated replacement, never missing, partial, or unknown bytes.
cases.expected_result: The target remains continuously readable as one of the two complete validated states on the tested platform and filesystem.

cases.purpose: Verify the CLI build script derives producer identity from its manifest worktree even when the process runs inside a different repository with redirected Git variables.

cases.purpose: Verify unknown signature handling does not make format or compatibility claims.

cases.expected_result: The CLI emits deterministic error JSON and a failure status.

cases.purpose: Verify independent raw-scan byte and page ceilings before page reads.

cases.distinct_invariant: A zero total-work limit rejects the decoder's one-unit shape inspection before reading or classifying the record.

cases.purpose: Verify out-of-range pages are rejected before any read.
cases.distinct_invariant: A page at the captured page count returns InvalidReference carrying the page and PageOutOfBounds source.

cases.distinct_invariant: With page visits exhausted, following a page returns a PageVisits read resource error without marking the page or advancing depth, and the same page follows under a fresh budget.

cases.purpose: Verify the visited set never grows past its reserved geometry.
cases.distinct_invariant: Marking reports first and repeat insertions exactly, and a page at the page count is rejected with PageOutOfBounds.
cases.expected_result: Membership queries outside the range are false and allocation is fixed.

cases.expected_result: Both typed locators preserve their exact row and page values with bounded work.

cases.purpose: Verify map locators are interpreted only in a classified table-definition page.
cases.distinct_invariant: A complete data page is rejected before either observed locator offset is decoded.

cases.purpose: Verify usage-map rows are located only on the expected classified data page.

cases.expected_result: The error identifies the expected and actual page context.

cases.purpose: Verify reverse-packed usage-map row boundaries.

cases.purpose: Verify the zero-row directory boundary.
cases.distinct_invariant: Row zero is rejected when the page declares no rows, before any directory entry is accessed.
cases.expected_result: The structured row-index error reports zero available rows.

cases.purpose: Verify exact slot-relative extended-page arithmetic boundaries.
cases.distinct_invariant: Bit 16,351 is accepted, bit 16,352 is rejected, and slot multiplication overflow is structured.

cases.expected_result: Traversal exhausts successfully after the table and record pages only.

cases.purpose: Verify record length, column count, name trailer, and object flag corruption paths.

cases.purpose: Verify fixed snapshot iteration over the complete commit region.

cases.expected_result: Forward, reverse, and indexed access agree for every slot and preserve all bytes.

cases.purpose: Verify retained vector capacity is charged from its actual element capacity before allocation.
cases.distinct_invariant: One retained u64 reserves one element and charges exactly its storage size, while a one-byte-short budget rejects before capacity changes.
cases.expected_result: The exact boundary yields capacity one and matching usage; one less leaves capacity and usage at zero.

cases.purpose: Verify contiguous property storage has a measurable exact allocation boundary.
cases.distinct_invariant: The first property precharges exactly one key/value slot without any opaque tree-node estimate, and insufficient budget cannot grow storage.
cases.expected_result: The exact slot-size limit succeeds with capacity one; one less fails with empty zero-capacity storage.

cases.purpose: Verify retained string growth accounts for existing spare capacity and the exact requested final capacity.
cases.distinct_invariant: Appending through partially used capacity charges only the final capacity delta, while a one-byte-short budget rejects before either capacity or content changes.
cases.expected_result: Capacity and usage both finish at five on the exact boundary; a four-byte limit preserves the prior two-byte content and four-byte capacity.

cases.purpose: Verify comparison-excluded external long-value headers retain an unambiguous canonical semantic association.
cases.distinct_invariant: A header for duplicate ordinal one resolves to that final row and an escaped Memo column token, while the retained binary value and raw_hex preserve the exact 12 bytes.
cases.expected_result: The producer extension key names canonical table 0, row 1, and the escaped value token, and both header fields equal the exact supplied bytes.

cases.purpose: Verify canonical row ordering keeps external long-value metadata attached to the exact duplicate row that supplied it.
cases.distinct_invariant: Rows arriving out of digest order are stably sorted, identical rows receive contiguous duplicate ordinals, and each distinct physical header is assigned the resulting canonical row index without a row-vector search.
cases.expected_result: The final ordinals are 0, 1, 0 and the three headers retain canonical row indexes 0, 1, and 2 with their original marker bytes.

cases.purpose: Verify the explicit canonical row-ordering work model excludes quadratic row-count growth.
cases.distinct_invariant: Doubling the modeled row count from 4,096 to 8,192 grows the two canonical-sort passes and one association pass by less than threefold rather than the fourfold growth of a full-vector scan per row.
cases.expected_result: The doubled work bound remains below three times the smaller bound, with zero and one-row boundaries equal to zero and one.

cases.purpose: Verify canonical row ordering and retained output share the caller's exact aggregate work ceiling.
cases.distinct_invariant: The measured total work for four duplicate rows succeeds unchanged at its exact limit while a one-unit-short aggregate budget rejects the operation.
cases.expected_result: The exact total-work ceiling succeeds with identical charged usage and one below returns an error.

cases.purpose: Verify public artifact serialization rejects a structurally large constructed model before walking its rows when the caller supplies a tiny budget.
cases.distinct_invariant: The validation boundary charges the complete row collection shape in constant time before canonical row validation can traverse any of the 20,000 constructed rows.
cases.expected_result: Serialization returns AllocationBytes while charged allocation and aggregate work remain within the 4,096-unit caller ceiling.

cases.purpose: Verify artifact validation applies the caller's decoded-text limits instead of an unrelated default budget.
cases.distinct_invariant: A valid retained Text value is conservatively precharged against both caller-supplied decoded-value ceilings before validation allocates or decodes its raw payload.
cases.expected_result: A zero decoded-value ceiling returns DecodedValueBytes and leaves cumulative decoded bytes at zero.

cases.purpose: Verify pre-publication Rust pair validation matches the shared validator's producer and scenario-branch admission boundary.
cases.distinct_invariant: A DAO-kind producer and a real successful database relabeled as an index scenario whose required branch was not traversed are both rejected after model validation but before artifact serialization.
cases.expected_result: Neither mismatched pair produces canonical artifact bytes that could reach bundle publication.

cases.purpose: Verify canonical row output storage is charged against the caller's allocation budget before the result vector can grow.
cases.distinct_invariant: The measured 128-row output allocation succeeds at its exact ceiling, while a one-byte-short ceiling rejects before any allocation is charged.
cases.expected_result: The exact allocation limit succeeds with matching usage; one less returns an error with zero charged allocation bytes.

cases.purpose: Verify composite-index scenario coverage cannot be inferred from definition shape without retained leaf-key evidence.
cases.distinct_invariant: An empty composite tree omits the lossless-key branch and makes the scenario receipt invalid, while a leaf entry with no key bytes is rejected by traversal before any receipt can be published.
cases.expected_result: Neither an empty tree nor a keyless entry can produce a canonical pair satisfying the composite scenario.

cases.purpose: Verify composite-index coverage is recorded after actual leaf traversal retains raw key bytes.
cases.distinct_invariant: A populated two-field index contributes the lossless-key branch only after both observed leaf entries retain nonempty raw composite key bytes.
cases.expected_result: The populated composite index emits the branch and its complete scenario-bound artifact pair serializes canonically.

cases.purpose: Verify decoded relationship cascade options project to the documented DAO relationship attribute bit field.
cases.distinct_invariant: No cascade emits 0, update-only emits 256, delete-only emits 4096, and combined cascade emits 4352 while the Boolean properties and canonical protocol 1.2 bytes agree with the same decoded options.
cases.expected_result: All four isolated cascade combinations produce their exact DAO attribute value and serialize that value in canonical relationship JSON.

cases.purpose: Verify database-wide producer-extension batching obeys the caller's exact aggregate-work ceiling.
cases.distinct_invariant: Fallible geometric growth, one canonical sort, and duplicate detection share one measured work bound for 1,024 retained extension entries.
cases.expected_result: The measured work ceiling succeeds exactly and one fewer work unit rejects before the uncharged operation can run.

cases.purpose: Verify producer-extension construction does not regain per-insertion vector shifting.
cases.distinct_invariant: Doubling a reverse-ordered extension batch from 4,096 to 8,192 entries grows charged construction and canonical-ordering work by less than threefold.
cases.expected_result: Both batches finish canonically and the doubled work remains below three times the smaller bound.

cases.purpose: Verify batched canonical producer extensions preserve unique-key enforcement.
cases.distinct_invariant: Two retained entries with the same JSON Pointer key are detected after the charged canonical sort and cannot construct a PropertyMap.
cases.expected_result: Finalization returns a structured protocol error instead of replacing either duplicate value.

cases.purpose: Verify completed semantic model ordering and validation share the caller's aggregate work ceiling.
cases.distinct_invariant: Canonical sorts and conservative validation lookup bounds are charged before finalization can reorder the completed model.
cases.expected_result: The exact measured ceiling succeeds and sorts the model, while one unit less returns TotalWorkUnits within budget and leaves the model unordered.

cases.purpose: Verify fixed-pair Rust serialization admits only coverage branches in the protocol 1.2 registry.
cases.distinct_invariant: An otherwise valid scenario-bound pair whose receipt is mutated with rows.imaginary fails before either canonical artifact is serialized.
cases.expected_result: Pair serialization returns a structured protocol-model error at the coverage receipt branch path.

cases.purpose: Verify the in-repository SHA-256 implementation against standard short vectors.
cases.distinct_invariant: Empty and abc inputs exercise padding with and without payload while producing exact 256-bit lowercase digests.
cases.expected_result: Both standard digests match byte for byte.

cases.purpose: Verify deterministic irregular incremental updates reproduce independently established SHA-256 digests across empty, boundary, multi-block, and larger inputs.
cases.distinct_invariant: Pseudo-random chunks of one through twenty-three bytes, interspersed with empty updates, must be equivalent to hashing each complete patterned input once.
cases.expected_result: All nine input lengths from zero through 1,024 bytes match their independent digests without chunk-boundary sensitivity.

cases.purpose: Verify buffered SHA-256 state survives many short updates that collectively cross one compression-block boundary.
cases.distinct_invariant: Eleven successive chunks totaling seventy bytes must preserve their exact order and buffered remainder across the 64-byte block transition.
cases.expected_result: Incremental hashing consumes the complete input and matches the independent whole-input digest.

cases.purpose: Verify every two-part update split reproduces independent SHA-256 vectors around block and padding boundaries.
cases.distinct_invariant: For patterned inputs of 55 through 65 bytes, all possible split positions plus an empty update must leave compression and final padding independent of update partitioning.
cases.expected_result: Every split of all eleven boundary lengths matches its independently established digest.

cases.purpose: Verify successful snapshot publication creates one complete bundle with implementation-owned artifact names.
cases.distinct_invariant: Snapshot and coverage bytes are durably staged and renamed together into snapshot.json and coverage-receipt.json during an ordinary uncontended publication.
cases.expected_result: Both fixed-name files contain their exact supplied bytes and the parent contains no bundle stage.

cases.purpose: Fault-inject every snapshot bundle publication step through the rename boundary.
cases.distinct_invariant: Under ordinary namespace conditions, failure before successful publication cannot expose a destination bundle or leak the unchanged stage entry, including a denied rename itself.
cases.expected_result: Every injected step returns an error with neither the destination nor a stage entry remaining.

cases.purpose: Verify snapshot bundle publication refuses all pre-existing destination entry identities.
cases.distinct_invariant: Regular files, directories, and hard links are detected without replacement, and rejecting a hard-linked destination cannot mutate its peer.
cases.expected_result: Each destination returns DestinationExists and the original hard-linked bytes remain unchanged.

cases.purpose: Verify dot-dot aliasing cannot disguise an existing input pathname as a snapshot bundle destination.
cases.distinct_invariant: Lexical normalization occurs before destination identity checks, so an alias resolving to the existing input cannot be staged or replaced.
cases.expected_result: Publication returns DestinationExists and preserves the input bytes exactly.

cases.purpose: Verify a non-existing destination containing a dot-dot component is normalized before staging and publication.
cases.distinct_invariant: The stage is created under the normalized parent and the final bundle appears only at the normalized destination without leaving an alias-local stage.
cases.expected_result: The fixed snapshot artifact is published under the normalized bundle path and no stage remains.

cases.purpose: Verify snapshot bundle publication rejects both live and dangling destination symlinks without following them.
cases.distinct_invariant: Symlink metadata is treated as an existing destination identity whether or not its target exists, preventing target traversal or link replacement.
cases.expected_result: Both symlink forms return DestinationExists and remain symlink entries.

cases.purpose: Verify a parent-directory sync failure after rename reports publication without claiming durability.
cases.distinct_invariant: Once the complete bundle rename has succeeded, a later parent sync error cannot be classified as an unpublished pre-rename failure.
cases.expected_result: The operation returns PublishedDurabilityUncertain while both fixed-name artifacts remain complete at the destination.

cases.purpose: Verify snapshot publication support and error reporting are explicit platform contracts.
cases.distinct_invariant: Linux, Apple, and Windows targets expose publication-stage errors, while every other target exposes only the fail-closed unsupported-platform error.
cases.expected_result: Platform preflight and every target-available error code match the declared platform contract.

cases.purpose: Verify a destination created by a competitor immediately before bundle rename wins without being overwritten.
cases.distinct_invariant: The atomic rename boundary detects the collision, preserves the competing directory and bytes, publishes none of the staged artifacts, and cleans the unchanged stage entry.
cases.expected_result: Publication returns RenameCollision, retains the competitor file, exposes no snapshot artifact, and leaves no stage.

cases.purpose: Replace the destination parent pathname after the stage descriptor is pinned, then exercise both successful publication and pre-rename cleanup.
cases.distinct_invariant: Artifact creation, synchronization, cleanup, and the no-replace rename remain relative to pinned parent and stage descriptors when the original parent is moved and a same-named stage is created under a replacement parent.
cases.expected_result: Success publishes both complete artifacts only under the moved pinned parent; injected failure removes the descriptor-pinned stage, while neither path writes to or removes the competitor stage under the replacement pathname.

cases.purpose: Replace the visible stage entry with forged fixed-name artifacts immediately before bundle publication continues.
cases.distinct_invariant: The atomic no-replace rename takes its source from the pinned outer-directory descriptor, so swapping the outer pathname cannot redirect publication to replacement bytes or authorize cleanup of the replacement.
cases.expected_result: Only the genuine snapshot and receipt reach the destination; the forged replacement remains byte-for-byte intact, the displaced opened anchor is empty, and publication reports cleanup uncertainty.

cases.purpose: Replace the visible stage entry with forged fixed-name artifacts and inject a failure at the publication boundary.
cases.distinct_invariant: Failure cleanup removes artifacts only through the pinned opened stage descriptors and refuses to remove or mutate the substituted outer pathname entry.
cases.expected_result: No destination is published; the forged replacement remains byte-for-byte intact, the displaced opened anchor is empty, and the operation reports cleanup uncertainty.

cases.purpose: Verify stage cleanup identity comparisons use the platform's native filesystem identity fields without numeric normalization.
cases.distinct_invariant: A retained directory descriptor matches its original device-and-inode entry but not a newly created entry at the same pathname after displacement.
cases.expected_result: The native identity comparison accepts the original entry and rejects the replacement entry.

cases.purpose: Verify Windows publication retains both staged artifact handles with later write sharing denied through the final staging boundary.
cases.distinct_invariant: Immediately before final validation and handle release, competing write opens for both synced artifacts are rejected; ordinary publication then atomically exposes the exact fixed pair after all rename-blocking handles close.
cases.expected_result: Both competing write opens fail at the rename hook, publication succeeds after final validation and handle release, and both destination artifacts contain their exact supplied bytes.

cases.purpose: Verify Windows publication treats live and dangling destination symlinks as existing identities without following them.
cases.distinct_invariant: The preflight uses symlink metadata before staging, so neither a valid target nor a missing target permits link traversal or replacement.
cases.expected_result: Both available symlink forms return DestinationExists and remain symlink entries; hosts lacking symlink privilege exit without weakening production behavior.

cases.purpose: Verify retargeting an input symlink after snapshot staging cannot redirect traversal to new source bytes.
cases.distinct_invariant: Traversal uses only the completed private staged storage rather than reopening the caller's original pathname after the copy.
cases.expected_result: After the alias is changed from the first file to the second, traversal still returns only the first file's staged bytes.

cases.purpose: Verify snapshot input staging enforces its byte limit at the exact boundary.
cases.distinct_invariant: An input exactly equal to max_bytes is copied completely, while a source one byte larger is rejected without truncation or partial success.
cases.expected_result: The exact seventeen-byte input reports length seventeen and matching bytes; the eighteen-byte input returns input_limit_exceeded.

cases.purpose: Verify the pathless-memory strategy is immutable after staging despite source mutation, truncation, unlink, and replacement.
cases.distinct_invariant: The one private memory copy and its digest are fixed while reading the already-open source and traversal borrows those exact bytes without reopening the original or making another full-size copy.
cases.expected_result: The staged digest matches the original content and memory-backed traversal returns the complete original bytes after every source-path change.

cases.purpose: Verify pathless-memory staging accepts its exact input boundary and fails closed on a deterministic fallible-reserve rejection.
cases.distinct_invariant: The declared input length is checked before allocation, every allocation is fallible, and a rejected initial capacity cannot produce partial staged success.
cases.expected_result: A seventeen-byte memory stage traverses exactly, while an injected sixteen-byte allocation ceiling returns input_stage_create_failed for the same input.

cases.purpose: Verify the non-Linux Unix fallback has no staging pathname that can adopt or delete an empty or nonempty replacement.
cases.distinct_invariant: Pathless memory removes both mkdir-to-open adoption and identity-check-to-cleanup races by construction; staging and close perform no operation on caller-created sentinel paths.
cases.expected_result: Traversal returns the exact staged bytes, close succeeds without pathname cleanup, and both the empty directory and the nonempty competitor remain unchanged.

cases.purpose: Verify each build reports the intended private staging strategy without claiming memory retention is filesystem-synced.
cases.distinct_invariant: Linux selects anonymous O_TMPFILE with fsync when available and otherwise pathless memory, Windows selects delete-on-close with fsync, and other targets select pathless memory explicitly marked not fsynced.
cases.expected_result: The compile-time strategy string exactly matches the active target family and distinguishes filesystem durability from memory retention.

cases.purpose: Verify slice and file out-of-range parity.
cases.distinct_invariant: Slice-backed and file-backed sources reject identical invalid ranges equivalently.
cases.expected_result: Both source types return the same structured boundary class.

cases.purpose: Verify empty source geometry and reading.
cases.distinct_invariant: Empty sources retain zero geometry and accept only an empty read at the end.
cases.expected_result: Slice and file sources agree without charging work.

cases.purpose: Verify file-source input length limits.
cases.distinct_invariant: File source construction accepts exact file capacity and rejects one byte above.
cases.expected_result: Oversize files return a structured input limit error.

cases.purpose: Verify stable file-source length.
cases.distinct_invariant: File length is captured once and later growth is not exposed through established geometry.
cases.expected_result: Reads beyond the captured length remain rejected.

cases.purpose: Verify source range arithmetic preflight.
cases.distinct_invariant: Offset-plus-length overflow is rejected before any underlying source access.
cases.expected_result: A structured arithmetic error is returned with zero I/O.

cases.purpose: Verify missing-file open diagnostics.
cases.distinct_invariant: Opening a missing source maps the platform failure to structured I/O context.
cases.expected_result: The error identifies the open operation and not-found kind.

cases.purpose: Verify source preflight accounting atomicity.
cases.distinct_invariant: Single and total read-limit failures leave the source budget unchanged.
cases.expected_result: No rejected preflight request consumes read budget.

cases.purpose: Verify successful slice/file source parity.
cases.distinct_invariant: Slice-backed and file-backed sources return identical bytes for identical valid ranges.
cases.expected_result: Returned bytes and work totals match across source implementations.

cases.purpose: Verify slice-source input length limits.
cases.distinct_invariant: Slice source construction accepts exact capacity and rejects one byte above.
cases.expected_result: Oversize slices return a structured input limit error.

cases.purpose: Verify shared operation accounting across readers.
cases.distinct_invariant: A source and binary cursor share and exhaust one enclosing operation budget.
cases.expected_result: Combined work cannot bypass the operation ceiling.

cases.purpose: Verify file truncation after length capture.
cases.distinct_invariant: A later-truncated file reports actual short-read bytes and charges attempted I/O.
cases.expected_result: The structured short-read error and budget reflect the failed access.

cases.purpose: Verify file-source random access initialization.
cases.distinct_invariant: Wrapping an open file is independent of its preexisting stream cursor position.
cases.expected_result: Absolute reads return the intended bytes regardless of prior cursor state.

cases.purpose: Verify immutable column and primary-index decoding.
cases.distinct_invariant: The parser retains sourced prefixes and records while exposing typed column storage, key direction, usage-map and non-traversed root references, and primary flags.
cases.expected_result: The synthetic Long column and primary index decode with exact raw and typed metadata.

cases.purpose: Verify lossless relationship metadata and isolated cascade options.
cases.distinct_invariant: All four observed update/delete option pairs remain raw while exposing their independently isolated booleans through an allocation-free relationship view.
cases.expected_result: The typed relationship retains name, side, ordinal, related TDEF, complete raw record, and exact cascade pair.

cases.purpose: Verify iterative TDEF continuation traversal and termination.
cases.distinct_invariant: An exact two-page definition succeeds while early termination, a repeated page, and a trailing link fail at distinct structured boundaries.
cases.expected_result: Only the exact chain returns an immutable definition and bounded raw suffix.

cases.purpose: Verify table and column count, ordinal, variable-counter, constant, and context invariants.
cases.distinct_invariant: Each corrupted sourced field is rejected instead of being normalized or guessed.
cases.expected_result: All controlled corruptions return structured table-definition errors.

cases.purpose: Verify the closed physical type inventory and column layout boundaries.
cases.distinct_invariant: Unknown types, unsupported type/class or size combinations, bad fixed offsets, and an invalid terminator fail closed.
cases.expected_result: No malformed column definition is emitted.

cases.purpose: Verify physical and logical index corruption boundaries.
cases.distinct_invariant: Invalid direction, key holes, unsupported flags, inconsistent selectors, and a wrong-kind root reference are rejected without tree traversal.
cases.expected_result: Every malformed index returns an index or reference-kind error.

cases.purpose: Verify exact table-definition allocation, item, and chain budgets.
cases.distinct_invariant: Observed exact capacities succeed while one-under allocation/item ceilings and one-under chain depth reject through the same operation budget.
cases.expected_result: All one-over resource cases fail with their precise limit kind.

cases.purpose: Verify every member of the closed observed physical type inventory and short-text size boundaries.
cases.distinct_invariant: All 13 accepted physical types, fixed Text, auto-increment Long, and Text sizes 1 and 255 decode while sizes 0 and 256 fail.
cases.expected_result: Only evidence-supported type, class, and size combinations produce column definitions.

cases.purpose: Verify count-driven truncation, duplicate key ordinals, and geometry reference boundaries.
cases.distinct_invariant: A one-over column count, repeated key column, and page-count index root each fail before producing an invalid immutable definition.
cases.expected_result: The parser returns structured truncation, duplicate-key, and invalid-reference errors.

cases.purpose: Verify the observed primary-table relationship selector remains distinct from the foreign-table selector.
cases.distinct_invariant: Marker one decodes only to PrimaryTable while retaining the same bounded related-table reference model.
cases.expected_result: The relationship metadata reports PrimaryTable without assigning cascade semantics.

cases.purpose: Verify table-definition header, logical-length, reserved-count, and continuation-prefix boundaries.
cases.distinct_invariant: Each invalid structural field is rejected before column or index metadata can be emitted.
cases.expected_result: All controlled header and continuation corruptions return their specific table-definition error.

cases.purpose: Verify the closed ordinary, primary, and relationship logical-index class invariants.
cases.distinct_invariant: Invalid selectors, context, relationship references, primary flags, classes, and physical ordinals fail closed while the valid ordinary class remains distinguishable.
cases.expected_result: Only the evidence-supported logical records decode and every mutation returns an index-definition error.

cases.purpose: Verify table and index definition errors retain public display context and nested causes.
cases.distinct_invariant: Plain format corruption exposes no synthetic source while index and resource wrappers preserve their cause.
cases.expected_result: Display and source behavior matches both structured definition error layers.

cases.purpose: Verify testkit fixture format metadata.
cases.distinct_invariant: Fixture metadata derives its format name from the production library scope.
cases.expected_result: Testkit and library report exactly the same scoped format name.

cases.purpose: Verify the pinned CP1252 discriminator and lossless raw retention.
cases.distinct_invariant: The distinguishing upper bytes map to their exact Unicode scalars while all source bytes remain available.
cases.expected_result: The decoded string and exact UTF-8 accounting match the public mapping table.

cases.purpose: Verify explicit CP1251 mappings and undefined-byte rejection.
cases.distinct_invariant: Selected boundary bytes decode exactly while an unmapped byte fails before resource counters advance.
cases.expected_result: Defined input decodes losslessly and undefined input returns its bounded index and byte.

cases.purpose: Verify text output is preflighted against decoded and allocation budgets.
cases.distinct_invariant: A multibyte Unicode result cannot be emitted or charged partially when its configured ceiling is too small.
cases.expected_result: The conversion fails with zero decoded output charged.

cases.purpose: Verify text errors retain public display context and nested resource causes.
cases.distinct_invariant: Undefined input exposes no synthetic source while resource rejection preserves its cause.
cases.expected_result: Display and source behavior matches the structured text error variant.

cases.purpose: Verify the observed scalar byte order and typed representations.
cases.distinct_invariant: Boolean, integer, floating, date, currency, and GUID values decode from exact-width sourced bytes without losing those bytes.
cases.expected_result: Every representative scalar matches its typed value and exact raw representation.

cases.purpose: Verify null, empty, and Boolean-presence distinctions.
cases.distinct_invariant: A cleared Boolean bit means false while a cleared non-Boolean presence bit means null, and present empty binary remains non-null.
cases.expected_result: All three physical states remain semantically distinct.

cases.purpose: Verify scalar width and decoded-byte resource boundaries.
cases.distinct_invariant: A malformed width is rejected structurally and an over-limit scalar is rejected before decoded accounting advances.
cases.expected_result: Neither invalid input produces a partial typed output.

cases.purpose: Verify value-decoding errors retain public display context and nested causes.
cases.distinct_invariant: Width failures expose no synthetic source while text and resource wrappers preserve their cause.
cases.expected_result: Display and source behavior matches the structured value error variant.
